one_month_reasoning: The main event in the window is Q3 2026 earnings. Intel has not announced the date: there is no 8-K on EDGAR and nothing on the IR calendar as of Oct 2 (src 22, 23). Last quarter's date was announced about 3 weeks ahead (Jun 30 for Jul 23), so an Oct 22-23 print is still the most likely; I put it about 85% inside the window. Guidance is $15.8-16.8B revenue, about 42% non-GAAP gross margin and $0.38 EPS. Consensus of $16.72B / $0.39 sits near the top of the range, after seven straight beats and a +34-40% September. The supervisor checked the reaction base rate: 8 of the last 11 next-day moves were negative, with a mean absolute move of about 11%. New since round 1: Intel's own 424B5 lock-up ends on the earlier of 90 days or the Q3 earnings release (src 4). With 2027 capex guided 'significantly above' 2026 (src 21), a follow-on or convertible right after the print is a real if unannounced possibility. That adds a little left skew. The 14A PDK 0.9 (October) could bring customer headlines and offsets some of that. I center at about $118.5 (slightly below spot) and use a fat-tailed 70/30 mix of 16% and 30% one-month sigmas, wider than annual vol / 3.5, because earnings fall in the window.

fair_value.method: Blend of three methods on 5.54B fully counted shares: 5.40B diluted plus the 143M DoC escrow shares, offset by about $3B of Secure Enclave cash received as they are released. Forward P/E: CY2028E EPS of $2.68 x 35x = $94. EV/sales: $80B x 7x less about $9B of net claims, including the $15.6B NCI = $99. SOTP: products $552B plus $75B for the foundry option and Mobileye, less about $16B of net claims = $110. Weighted 40/30/30, that gives about $100.

I then divide by 1.026 for the 143M escrowed DoC shares. The 424B5 excludes them from the outstanding count and releases them as Secure Enclave disbursements arrive (src 4).

Large-cap semi peer range (NVDA 28x, TSMC ~23x average, src 12).

Mobileye stake about $7B. Foundry option raised from about $53B to about $68B because two findings firm up the timeline. First, the CEO's Q2 remarks confirm 14A risk production in H2 2027 and a full commit to HVM in 2028 (src 21). Second, Kuo reports Apple has signed an NDA and is qualifying 18A-P for its base M-series chip (src 24); neither company has confirmed it. I stay well below the $110-120B the supervisor found better supported, because external foundry revenue was only $293M in Q2 (src 7), no 14A customer has committed (src 14), and the foundry still loses about $2.5B a quarter.

bear.story: Supply catches up in 2027 and agentic-AI CPU demand cools or shifts to Arm and AMD. Server pricing reverses. No 14A anchor customer is signed, and the Apple 18A-P qualification stays small or lapses. 2027 capex well above 2026 pushes FCF negative, and a post-lock-up equity raise after the Q3 print dilutes holders. EPS lands around $2.0 at 30-35x.

base.story: Intel keeps beating while supply-constrained. Gross margin reaches the mid 40s and CY2028 EPS of about $2.9 becomes visible. 14A risk production starts on schedule in H2 2027, and one or two partial external engagements (Apple 18A-P, EMIB-T) are disclosed. The multiple compresses from about 60x toward 38-40x forward, so the stock roughly holds.

bull.story: A binding 14A anchor customer (Apple, Nvidia or a hyperscaler) is named after the October PDK 0.9. Apple confirms 18A-P. EMIB-T adds billions from H2 2027 and foundry reaches breakeven by end-2027. CY2028 EPS above $4 at about 45x. This scenario carries wide dispersion (about 38%), so outcomes of $250-300+ keep real weight.

thesis_break_reason: $72 is about 24% below the $95 August offering price, where the CEO bought, and below the July 2026 low near $82. That low is where ordinary de-rating alone stopped. At $72 the stock would be about 35x 2027 EPS on a fully counted basis, roughly a peer multiple. Getting there most likely takes falling estimates: the server-CPU upcycle and pricing turning, or the 14A anchor decision going against Intel. I keep $72 rather than the supervisor's $70; the $2 gap is within noise and my reasoning is the same.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor confirmed my round-1 offering and share facts and graded my sourcing high. I acted on its three points. (1) Escrow shares. I verified in the 424B5 that 143M DoC shares sit in escrow, are excluded from the 5,285M post-offering count, and are released as Secure Enclave disbursements arrive. I now count 5.54B shares and credit about $3B of linked cash, for a net drag of about $2/share. (2) NCI. The 424B5 capitalization table shows $15.6B at 6/27/26, against the $13.4B I used. (3) Lock-up. The company lock-up ends at the earlier of 90 days or the Q3 release, so I dated the raise-risk catalyst. EDGAR shows no filing since 8/12, and Intel has not announced the Q3 date. The supervisor's 14A finding matches the Q2 prepared remarks I re-read (risk production H2 2027, HVM commit 2028). Together with Kuo's report of Apple qualifying 18A-P, it led me to raise the foundry option from $60B to $75B, still below the $110-120B the supervisor called better supported, because external revenue is $293M a quarter and no commitment exists. Net fair value moved from $102 to $100: P/E $94, EV/sales $99, SOTP $110. Ladder: the same three-scenario lognormal mixture ($66/30%, $115/45%, $190/25%). I widened the bull dispersion to 38% and the bear to 38%. The supervisor was right that my $300 tail (1.5%) was inconsistent with my own bull case, and the corrected mixture gives about 3%. I keep it below the others' 5-7% because the fundamentals still put fair value under spot. I also lowered P(>=30) to 0.985 for crash risk at 76% vol. Median is about $111, with P(>=120) at about 44%.
